column1: # NARROW.tsv -- graded, but by a comparison NARROWER than the claim the percent makes.
# name<TAB>NARROWING<TAB>reason.  lib_inventory.sh: "AN UNEXPLAINED BUCKET IS JUST A SMALLER LIE" (hq_P).
# ⭐ WHAT THE INSTRUMENT SEES.  These programs self-check: math_chks.inc's chks(expression,expected) EVALs
# the expression, compares it against the expected value, and prints its own verdict -- " pass: <expr>
# Obs[..] Exp[..]" or "*FAIL: ... (exception)".  test_snobol4_spitbol_x64_suite.sh grades them by reading
# those lines: SCRIP must print zero "*FAIL:" and exactly as many " pass:" as the oracle printed on the
# same program in the same run.  Any wrong arithmetic result makes the program itself say *FAIL:, so the
# instrument's sensitivity is NOT below the effect it exists to detect.
# ⛔ WHAT IT DOES NOT SEE, which is why these are narrow and not stream: the Obs[] and Exp[] TEXT.  Two
# engines that agree to 1e-12 (chks's own tolerance) but print 0.263083649990256e-307 against
# 2.6308364999025599e-308 both print " pass:", and this instrument cannot tell them apart.  That
# insensitivity is deliberate -- the row asks for it, because a byte diff would call a float formatting
# difference a defect -- but a reader of the percent is owed the fact that it is there.
# ⭐ THE SET IS MEASURED, NOT LISTED: the runner picks the arm from whether the ORACLE's own run printed
# verdict lines, and cross-checks this file against what it measured, both directions, every run.  It said
# so on the spot -- this file was written with 8 entries and the very next run, on the tree where hq_C's
# case-conversion row had landed, printed "⚠ NARROW.tsv UNRECORDED ... math_atan.sbl math_chop.sbl ..." and
# the inventory REFUSED(2) on graded_narrow=17 against 8 declared.  The nine below were added on that
# measurement.  ⛔ Nothing here may be inferred at run time; the runner may only disagree out loud.
math_diff.sbl
